about:
One operation on an index's text, as the tree and the index view ask for it. Only the lines moved or changed are touched: bullets, indentation, line endings and a byte order mark stay. An entry is named by its child's name (child-name, letter case aside; the first entry naming it) or by { line } (for any entry, including one whose link names no child). input: { text, op } → expected new text, or null when nothing changes or it is not possible. Operations (kind):
- move { ref, target, place: before | after | into, folder }: the entry with its sub-list put before or after the target (and its sub-list), or into it as its last sub-item (indented as the target's sub-items are, else to the target's text column; in a tab-nested index with a tab). Not into itself or its own sub-list. A child not listed yet gets a new entry '<marker> [title](href)' (marker: a bullet as the target's, or the next number in a numbered list; title: entry-title; href: href with folder).
- insert { name, folder, title, under, after }: a new entry for a child not listed: as the last sub-item of 'under', right after 'after' (and its sub-items), or after the last top-level entry; in a file without entries, a '- ' list at the end after a blank line. A title given is used (brackets and backslashes escaped).
- remove { ref, subtree }: the entry's line; its sub-items move up a level into its place, or go with it (subtree).
- indent { ref, folders }: the entry (with its sub-items) becomes the last sub-item of the entry before it at its level. Only notes nest: neither entry may be a folder's (link ending in '/', a link to a folder's index, or a child named in 'folders').
- outdent { ref }: the entry (with its sub-items) goes right after its parent's sub-list, at the parent's level.
- shift { ref, step }: past the entry before (step < 0) or after (otherwise) at its level.
- rename { from, to, title }: links to the child follow (every link in the file, anchors, angle brackets and encoding kept); with title, each entry naming the child gets it; without, an entry whose text was the old entry-title gets the new one.
- retitle { ref, title }: the entry's text set (trimmed, white space collapsed, brackets and backslashes escaped); a blank title is refused.
